article.title: Ukraine’s Drone Offensive Gives Kyiv a 3-to-1 Edge Over Russia
article.summary: Major Ukrainian attacks have frequently involved hundreds, and at times more than a thousand, drones directed at military, industrial, and energy targets across Russia. By contrast, Russian strikes have generally relied on smaller numbers of drones supplemented by missiles. Even so, Ukraine appears to be launching several times more long-range strike drones at targets inside Russia than Moscow is sending in the opposite direction.

article.title: Putin Accuses Kyiv of Striking Polling Stations: ‘We Were Ready to Resume Negotiations’
article.summary: Speaking to reporters on Friday, Russian President Vladimir Putin again pinned the blame for stalled diplomacy on Ukraine, saying Moscow was ready to resume negotiations after its Sept. 18-20 State Duma elections. He claimed Ukraine attacked the country’s polling stations, and added that the proposals for a peaceful settlement still exist – after the Kremlin decides “what is in its interests.” Putin’s remarks came as Washington stepped up its effort to broker an end to the war.

article.title: Russian State Media Deletes Opinion Piece Calling for Attack on Lithuania

article.title: Putin says Russia will not attack Europe and blames Ukraine for the breakdown in peace talks
article.summary: Shortly before the State Duma elections, Ukraine said it was ready to return to negotiations. Russia was prepared to resume contact after the elections. But on the main voting day, Kyiv attacked Moscow, launched more than 1,600 drones, and struck polling stations. After what they did, we’ll consider how to respond. We’ll decide whether to resume negotiations based on our own interests. Ukraine must feel the effects of Russia’s retaliatory strikes. The strikes are so destructive that Ukraine is raising the prospect of a ceasefire and trying to stop Russia’s “Geran” drone strikes. Kyiv’s provocations only make things worse for Ukraine. Russia is not preparing for military action against Europe; we have no such plans. European countries themselves are escalating tensions and engaging in provocations. article.title: Raging Putin’s Table-Slamming Meltdown Revealed
article.summary: Anastasia Barashkova / REUTERSThe Wall Street Journal reporter who spent 16 months behind bars in Russia has revealed that Vladimir Putin once exploded in a fit of rage while talking about him.Evan Gershkovich, released in 2024 after a grueling 491 days in custody,writesthat he has since uncovered what likely led to his arrest—and Putin’s visceral private reaction when pressed on whether he should have ever been detained as a foreign agent at all.In an excerpt from a forthcoming book, Gershkovich reveals that Putin slammed a table and yelled that the New Jersey-born reporter was an “idiot” in response to a world leader expressing doubt that Russia could have arrested Gershkovich so easily if he was truly a spy, as Moscow alleged.Read more at The Daily Beast.
